data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The largest of the three consecutive even integers is 48, derived by exploiting the algebraic identity that the arithmetic mean of an odd-length symmetric arithmetic progression equals its central term (n/3), so the middle term is 46 and the largest is 48.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the arithmetic mean 138/3 = 46 were odd, the triple would be consecutive odd integers, violating the evenness constraint and yielding no valid solution","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the problem asked for consecutive integers with a different common difference d, the mean would still be 46 but the largest term would be m + d rather than 48","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"For three consecutive even integers with common difference 2, model them as (m-2, m, m+2).
